newsitem.title: UK: Hanson makes H1 profit of 47.8 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Hanson makes H1 profit of 47.8 mln stg.

text.p: British-based materials and services group Hanson Plc said on Thursday that it made pro-forma half year pretax profits of 47.8 million pounds ($75.8 million) and would pay an interim dividend of four pence per share.

Hanson, which inherits the name of the once-mighty conglomerate which completed its demerging earlier this year, also announed that it expects to pay a final dividend of eight pence per share. "The rate of improvement in operating profit showed an increasing trend in the June quarter and Hanson is now moving forward in accordance with its long-term plan," said chairman Lord Hanson in a statement.

Pro-forma operating profits for the six months to June 30, 1997 rose nine percent to 121 million pounds. The pretax profit figure of 47.8 million was derived after the company took a charge of 49 million, which included a 28 million book loss on the sale of Hanson Electrical.

Hanson said that the company's U.S. interests were helped by the strength of the U.S. economy. The firm said the recovery was increasing in its UK companies, although it noted this recovery had flattened in recent weeks.

The company warned that the UK government's recent cancellation of a number of road schemes and delays to others would affect its building materials unit ARC. Operating profits at ARC rose six percent to 45.4 million pounds.
The pound's meteoric rise on the foreign exchanges hit the company's translation of European and foreign earnings by 4.4 million pounds at the profit level.
